messages:
Maria: Quick sync — we need to finalize the FlashAttention v2/v3 kernel gating + KV/paged fallback playbook before the canary tomorrow. TL;DR: v3 improves short/medium seq latency but we saw a 4% tail regression on long-prompt paged-KV cases in last perf run.

Lee: ack. do we have a repro profile?

Sam: I captured a profile on staging. gist: https://redwood.gists/flashv3-longseq-profile (only internal). Key callout: v3 kernel introduces extra memcpy for paged-KV hotpath when seq_len>2048 and page-evictions happen.

Devon: that memcpy explains the tail. is it happening every request or only when eviction occurs?

Sam: only on page-refill events. steady-state cached requests look fine. but our 95/99 p50s for long running chats spike when the refill rate > ~5/s per model instance.

Maria: proposal: gate v3 by two flags: kernel_selector=auto_v3 and paged_kv_guard=enabled. Rollout phases: 1) canary (5% traffic, low-concurrency instances), 2) burst-sim canary (synthetic long seq traffic), 3) regional ramp (50%), 4) global.

Lee: add telemetry breakouts for: kernel_used, paged_kv_evictions, memcpy_ns_per_refill, model_seq_len_bucket. Need dashboards and alert thresholds.

Devon: suggested alert: if canary 95p latency > baseline + 3% OR paged_kv_evictions rate > 2x baseline -> auto rollback. Good?

ryan_opsbot: note: rollback automation requires tag "flashv3_canary" on the deployment and the rollback playbook to be uploaded to /playbooks/flashv3_rollback.md

Maria: yes. also plan a fallback kernel that avoids the memcpy path: revert to fused-attn kernel on paged contexts. fallback rules: if paged_kv_evictions > threshold OR memcpy_ns/refill > 200us -> route to fused-attn for seq>1024.

Sam: benchmark numbers from yesterday: short seq (<=256): v3 median -6% latency, long seq (>=2048): v3 p99 +4% on paged workloads. fused-attn p99 is +8% vs v2 but no eviction memcpy. So tradeoff is predictable higher cost vs occasional spikes.

Lee: for rollout flags, propose names: rtx.flash.kernel_selector = "auto_v3"
rfx.flash.paged_kv_guard = "enabled"
rfx.flash.paged_kv_thresholds = "evictions:10/min,memcpy_ns:200000"

Devon: include a perf litmus test in canary step: run synthetic chat with interleaved cache-eviction pattern (span=30s, random writes) for 15m, measure p95/p99 and eviction count. If failure -> rollback.

Maria: ops playbook outline (short):
- Start canary via deploy-bot (tag flashv3_canary).
- Monitor dashboard: kernel_used, memcpy_ns, KV_evictions, p95/p99 latency.
- If alert triggers, run -> deploy-bot rollback flashv3_canary -> notify #incidents and paging list.
- If borderline, enable paged_kv_guard=false for the canary subset to force fused fallback and retest.

ryan_opsbot: deploy-bot: canary deployment started for service=runtime-modelpool-3 region=us-west-2 tag=flashv3_canary

Lee: small config snippet for the rollout API: 
POST /admin/feature_flags
{
  "service": "runtime",
  "flag": "rtx.flash.kernel_selector",
  "value": "auto_v3",
  "scope": "pool:canary-5pct"
}

Sam: leaving a note: during canary, collect raw nvml traces + malloc stats. Sam will run a focused mem-alloc flamegraph if we see >2x memcpy_ns spikes.

Devon: who is oncall for the canary window tomorrow 14:00-16:00 PT?

Maria: oncall: Devon, backup: Sam. I'll be monitoring dashboards.

Lee: I'll push the dashboard tiles by EOD. Tagging @Devon for any final constraints. :eyes: 

Devon: sounds good. I'll prepare the litmus job and the rollback playbook.

Maria: thanks all. if anyone finds new regressions or alternate mitigations (kernel micro-patch to avoid the extra memcpy) drop them here. otherwise we'll run canary tomorrow and reconvene after 16:30 PT. :thumbsup:
